items.headline: Stocks fell Monday as investors braced for Nvidia's earnings
items.note: All three major indexes closed lower on Nov. 16, with the Nasdaq falling the most and the Dow the least. Reports put the Nasdaq's drop between roughly 1.7% and 2.5%, so I'm not quoting an exact figure. Selling centered on AI-linked stocks.

items.headline: Nvidia reports earnings today after the close
items.note: Analysts expect about $109 billion in revenue and adjusted EPS near $2.47, with gross margin guided to 74%. It's the first report since Jensen Huang's exit, and the stock is about 30% below its record high. Nvidia's results set the tone for AI spending and hiring.

items.headline: CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a successor
items.note: Kress, CFO since 2013, is running the company temporarily after Huang resigned. Watch what she says on today's call about the Vera Rubin ramp and China demand.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO is expected to price Wednesday and trade Thursday
items.note: The expected timeline is pricing on Nov. 18 and Nasdaq trading as ANT on Nov. 19, subject to regulatory clearance and market conditions. The range is $70–$78 a share for about 825 million shares.

items.headline: The Anthropic offering could raise up to $64.4 billion
items.note: Reports say the deal could raise up to $64.4 billion, with the range midpoint implying a valuation near $1 trillion. That would make it one of the largest IPOs ever, and a big test of public appetite for AI companies.

items.headline: Hot inflation data has pushed Treasury yields up and kept Fed hike talk alive
items.note: Treasury futures pointed to higher yields after hot October inflation. As of late October, markets saw a December quarter-point hike as likely, though odds move with each data release. Higher yields tend to pressure tech valuations.

items.headline: Tech layoffs keep rising in 2026, but data and AI skills stay in demand
items.note: Trackers count well over 140,000 to 200,000+ tech job cuts this year, with new cuts at Canva, Squarespace and Block. Analyses say specialized data roles hold up better than junior or generalist ones, so build concrete project experience for 2027 internships.

learn.explain: After a company goes public, early investors and employees usually can't sell their shares right away. This waiting period, often around 90 to 180 days, is called the lock-up. It exists so a flood of insiders selling doesn't crash the price just as outside investors are buying in. When a lock-up ends, a lot of new shares can hit the market, and the stock sometimes dips. Anthropic's expected IPO this week will have one, so insiders holding shares won't be able to sell right away.
learn.try: Look up when the lock-up ends for a recent big IPO and see how the stock behaved around that date.
